newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire rebels say they have seized Goma airport.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say they have seized Goma airport.

text.p: Tutsi rebels on Thursday claimed to have captured the eastern Zaire airport of Goma, centre of relief operations for more than a million Hutu refugees.
A rebel spokesman in the rebel-held Zairean town of Uvira said there was heavy fighting in Goma about 250 km (150 miles) to the north and warned aid agencies not to use the airport.

"Goma airport is under the control of our military forces," Laurent Kabila, chief coordinator of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, told a Reuters correspondent in Uvira.
Warning aid agencies and others, he said: "They would be doing so at their own risk because of the heavy fighting in Goma.
"Goma is in the process of falling as I talk to you. Government forces are running away. There is a big battle going on in Goma and within two days we will have full control of the city."
Zairean authorities gave contradictory accounts on Thursday of whether they still held Goma airport, first telling U.N. officials it had fallen and then saying it had not.
Steve Pratt, an official with CARE International, told Reuters aid agencies had been told to prepare for a partial or total evacuation from Goma by road to neighbouring Rwanda.
